column1: # RFC-0188 P0.1/P0.3 — formal depth ratchet (floors + cap + series).
# The proof ladder is extract -> close -> atom (RFC-0188 background).
#   floor_extract/floor_close/floor_atom are FLOORS: actual depth below
#   floor = red (a proof regressed). Floors only move UP, in the SAME
#   commit as the proof that earns the move.
#   cap_data_fate is a CAP: more data-fate atoms in glue = red. It only
#   moves DOWN (trampoline monotonicity; reductions keep landing per fire).
#   handler_loc is a recorded SERIES (not enforced): move it in the same
#   commit as a trampoline change; the diff is the review artifact.
# close/atom proofs are REGISTERED in close_proofs.tsv (the ladder credit);
# floor_close/floor_atom count REGISTERED proofs. residuals.json
# proof_depth counts registered proofs + unregistered close/atom twins
# without extraction (pedra_formal.py rule) and must EQUAL that live count.
# RFC-0188 P1.6 registered visible_at atom (0085e919) moving one pair from
# extract to atom; the extract freeze went stale there (276 frozen vs 275
# live) — P1.5 recounts it honestly and moves floor_extract to 275 in the
# SAME commit (a ladder promotion, not a lost extraction).
# RFC-0199 adds the `count` credit (work-count theorem over an Aeneas
# extract): floor_count counts REGISTERED count rows and only moves UP,
# in the SAME commit as the theorem. Count is orthogonal to the ladder —
# a pair may carry close AND count. residuals proof_depth.count equals
# the live count of registered count rows.
floor_extract 200
floor_close 6
floor_atom 78
floor_count 7
cap_data_fate 46
handler_loc 111927
